subsystems.name: Well field
subsystems.role: one or more deep boreholes that reach hot rock and carry water down and back up.

subsystems.name: Reservoir (the rock itself)
subsystems.role: a engineered fracture network in hot, low-permeability rock that lets water sweep across a large hot surface area.

subsystems.name: Stimulation system
subsystems.role: creates and maps the permeability that nature did not provide.

subsystems.name: Downhole pumps and completion
subsystems.role: lift hot brine to the surface where pressure or depth is insufficient.

subsystems.name: Grid connection and water management
subsystems.role: delivers power and handles the fluid loop.

buildSteps.title: Explore and baseline the site
buildSteps.detail: Temperature gradient wells, rock sampling, stress measurements and seismic monitoring establish how hot the rock is and how it is likely to fracture.

buildSteps.title: Drill the first deep well
buildSteps.detail: A rotary rig drills 2–4 km of hard crystalline rock, steering the hole with directional tools; casing is cemented in stages to seal groundwater.

buildSteps.title: Stimulate the rock
buildSteps.detail: Water is injected at pressures high enough to shear existing fractures and open flow paths, usually in several stages along the well. Seismic sensors track every event so pumping can be stopped if it grows too strong.

buildSteps.title: Drill the second well
buildSteps.detail: A production well is drilled into the same hot volume, aimed to intersect the stimulated fracture network and form a connected pair.

buildSteps.title: Test circulation
buildSteps.detail: Water is pumped from the injection well to the production well for weeks or months, measuring flow rate, produced temperature and how much pressure is needed.

buildSteps.title: Build the surface plant
buildSteps.detail: Hot brine passes through heat exchangers that boil a low-boiling-point working fluid, which spins a turbine; the cooled fluid is reinjected.

buildSteps.title: Connect and expand
buildSteps.detail: Power goes to the grid, while more wells are drilled from the same pad to share roads, rig moves and pipelines. Long-term seismic and reservoir monitoring continues.

prerequisites.why: the oil and gas industry already drills kilometres of steered hole, but rarely in hot granite.
electronics, seals and motors degrade quickly above about 200 °C.
drilling typically dominates the cost of a project, so cheap metres are the key to competitiveness.
they generate electricity from fluids well below boiling point, matching EGS temperatures.
large felt earthquakes have shut projects down, so operators must keep events small and predictable.
you need to know where the fractures went before deciding where to drill next.

pathway.milestone: pilot plants proving that a drilled and stimulated well pair can deliver steady power to a grid
pathway.unlocks: a repeatable design for a commercial-scale well field.

pathway.milestone: multi-well pads and drilling-learning curves that cut cost per megawatt
pathway.unlocks: EGS that competes with other firm low-carbon generation in ordinary rock.

pathway.milestone: reuse of existing deep oil and gas wells and infrastructure
pathway.unlocks: faster, cheaper deployment using holes that are already drilled.

pathway.milestone: superhot-rock drilling above roughly 400 °C, in some concepts with millimetre-wave or other novel drilling methods
pathway.unlocks: several times more power per well and geothermal almost anywhere.
